title: Identity-compactification normalization of the specified total-limit comparison maps
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_m=R/\varpi^m$ for $m\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y_0$ be proper over $k_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $a:Y\to s$, $g_Y$ and $g_s$ be its structure map and geometric Frobenii [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Use $c=(\operatorname{id}_Y,a)$ at every level. For $M\in D^b_c(Y,R)$ use the strict-system reduction $\mathcal R_YM$, simultaneous operations $\mathcal F_a,\mathcal G_Y,\mathcal G_s,\mathcal J=\mathcal J_{\operatorname{id}_Y}$ and $\mathcal L_s=R\varprojlim\circ U_s$ of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; $U_s$ restricts each coefficient to the completed integral coefficient sheaf. Let $u:\mathcal J\xrightarrow{\sim}1$ be the canonical identity-open identification furnished by sheafification [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $\kappa_M:Ra^c_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_*M$ be the actual identity-compactification comparison [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence], obtained by total limit of the identity-open comparison of strict quotient-transition towers [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Write $M'=Lg_Y^*M$ using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Denote by $\alpha_!,\beta_!,\alpha_*,\beta_*$ exactly the canonical operation-comparison maps in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], including their specified units and counits. Set
$$h_S=\mathcal G_s\mathcal F_a(u_{\mathcal R_YM}),\qquad h_T=\mathcal F_a(u_{\mathcal G_Y\mathcal R_YM}).$$
Thus $h_S$ maps the compact system source to the ordinary system source, and $h_T$ maps the compact system target to the ordinary system target. The following are equalities of the specified comparison morphisms:
$$\mathcal L_s(h_S)\circ\alpha_!(M)=\alpha_*(M)\circ Lg_s^*(\kappa_M),$$
$$\kappa_{M'}\circ\beta_!(M)=\beta_*(M)\circ\mathcal L_s(h_T).$$
They identify the comparison maps themselves through whole-system identity-open cancellation, with all quotient transitions retained. Their scalar-localized images are the canonical comparisons for $E$; their common finite coefficient-field representatives are the canonical comparisons for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with the localization and common-stage conventions of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange].

proof.text: First check domains. The map $a$ is the base change of the proper structure map of $Y_0$, hence is proper. The inverses of $g_Y,g_s$ are obtained by replacing geometric with arithmetic Frobenius; they are scheme isomorphisms, without any assertion of $k$-linearity. Thus $M'=Lg_Y^*M$ is integral constructible, and $Ra_*M$ and $Ra_*M'$ are integral constructible by the integral direct-image theorem. The identity compactification is therefore available for both inputs. All subsequent system operations are on the ordinary derived categories of the small pro-etale system sites specified in the statement.

source.place: Step 6 (proper case), agent expansion: properness and domains

proof.text: For $N=M,M'$ put $Q_N^c=\mathcal F_a\mathcal J\mathcal R_YN$, $Q_N=\mathcal F_a\mathcal R_YN$, and $v_N=\mathcal F_a(u_{\mathcal R_YN})$. Apply the current proper integral tower comparison with $X=Y$, target $s$, and $f=a$: both schemes are separated finite-type over $k$, $a$ is a proper $k$-morphism, and both inputs are integral constructible by step 1. Its fixed strict models are $T_!^0=U_s\mathcal F_a\mathcal J\mathcal R_Y$ and $T_*=U_s\mathcal F_a\mathcal R_Y$, with total limit $R\lim$, exactly the $\mathcal L_s=R\lim\circ U_s$ convention here. The system-mate statement supplies the section-normalized $u$ on whole systems, retaining every quotient transition and restriction comparison. Hence $U_s(v_N)$ is the identity-open tower isomorphism in the fixed model of the proper integral tower comparison, whose limit is the actual proper comparison. Thus $Ra_!^cN=\mathcal L_sQ_N^c$, $Ra_*N=\mathcal L_sQ_N$, and $\kappa_N=\mathcal L_s(v_N)$; in particular $h_S=\mathcal G_s(v_M)$. The coefficient sheaf throughout is the completed integral sheaf. These are whole-system functor identifications with the fixed natural limit projections; equality is not inferred from finite evaluations or from a choice of Roos triangle.

source.place: Step 6 (proper case), agent expansion: the actual identity-open comparison on strict quotient towers

proof.text:
Write $\epsilon_Q:\mathcal R_s\mathcal L_sQ\to Q$ for the counit of the reduction/total-limit adjunction, and $r_s(K):Lg_s^*K\to\mathcal L_s\mathcal G_s\mathcal R_sK$ for the primitive completed-pullback realization. The primitive comparison lemma supplies this natural $r_s$, with its actual quotient transitions and natural Roos comparison. The system evaluation calculus supplies $\epsilon$ as a natural transformation before evaluation. The exchange definition forms its source comparisons by the integral realization of [def-weil-system-operation-exchange-realization]: alpha is the recorded pullback realization followed by the whole-system counit $\mathcal R\mathcal L\to1$. Unpacking this gives
$$\alpha_!(M)=\mathcal L_s\mathcal G_s(\epsilon_{Q_M^c})\circ r_s(\mathcal L_sQ_M^c),\qquad
\alpha_*(M)=\mathcal L_s\mathcal G_s(\epsilon_{Q_M})\circ r_s(\mathcal L_sQ_M).$$
Indeed the first arrow realizes completed pullback on the defining reduction tower; the second replaces the reduction of its total limit by the original direct-image system using the adjoint of the limit projections. This is exactly the operation comparison with its specified counit, since operation reduction preserves those counits. This description uses natural transformations on whole systems; it needs no conservativity assertion for evaluation on morphisms.

source.place: Step 6 (proper case), agent expansion: unpack the alpha comparisons as the primitive realization followed by the system counit

proof.text:
Apply naturality of $\epsilon$ to $v=v_M$: $v\circ\epsilon_{Q_M^c}=\epsilon_{Q_M}\circ\mathcal R_s\mathcal L_s(v)$. Apply $\mathcal L_s\mathcal G_s$, and then naturality of $r_s$ to $\mathcal L_s(v)$. The formulas in the preceding step give
$$\mathcal L_s\mathcal G_s(v)\circ\alpha_!(M)
=\mathcal L_s\mathcal G_s(\epsilon_{Q_M})\circ r_s(\mathcal L_sQ_M)\circ Lg_s^*\mathcal L_s(v)
=\alpha_*(M)\circ Lg_s^*(\kappa_M).$$
Using $h_S=\mathcal G_s(v)$ proves the first required equality.

source.place: Step 6 (proper case), agent expansion: alpha equality by two naturality squares

proof.text:
Let $d_M:\mathcal R_YM'\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G_Y\mathcal R_YM$ be the canonical coherent pullback/reduction comparison. The integral pullback-system comparison gives this natural isomorphism with the actual adjoints of the Roos projections. By [def-weil-system-operation-exchange-realization], used in the exchange definition, beta is the inverse of this canonical reduction/pullback counit, realized through the system direct image. Unpacking the specified target operation comparisons gives
$$\beta_*(M)=\mathcal L_s\mathcal F_a(d_M^{-1}),\qquad
\beta_!(M)=\mathcal L_s\mathcal F_a\mathcal J(d_M^{-1}).$$
Here the ordinary target is $\mathcal L_s\mathcal F_a\mathcal R_YM'=Ra_*M'$, and the compact target is $\mathcal L_s\mathcal F_a\mathcal J\mathcal R_YM'=Ra_!^cM'$. The open functor acts on the same system comparison $d_M^{-1}$: reduction is performed on the input before open extension in the compact-support definition. The operation-reduction theorem ensures that these are the recorded comparisons with their units and counits, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms between the displayed objects.

source.place: Step 6 (proper case), agent expansion: unpack beta using the coherent pullback/reduction comparison

proof.text:
Naturality of the section-normalized system isomorphism $u:\mathcal J\to1$ at $d_M^{-1}$ gives
$$u_{\mathcal R_YM'}\circ\mathcal J(d_M^{-1})=d_M^{-1}\circ u_{\mathcal G_Y\mathcal R_YM}.$$
Apply $\mathcal F_a$ and the total-limit functor. With the preceding beta formulas and $\kappa_{M'}=\mathcal L_s\mathcal F_a(u_{\mathcal R_YM'})$, this becomes
$$\kappa_{M'}\circ\beta_!(M)=\beta_*(M)\circ\mathcal L_s\mathcal F_a(u_{\mathcal G_Y\mathcal R_YM})=\beta_*(M)\circ\mathcal L_s(h_T).$$
Functoriality applies to these equal whole-system maps, so every quotient transition is retained.

source.place: Step 6 (proper case), agent expansion: beta equality by the naturality square of identity-open cancellation

proof.text: For $E$ apply scalar localization to the two equalities just proved. Functors preserve composition and equality. The exchange definition specifies the field comparisons as precisely these images. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ represent all objects and maps at one common finite coefficient field and take their common-stage classes. The operation-reduction comparisons commute with this coefficient passage, so the images are the canonical comparisons stipulated in the statement. No rational object is reduced modulo a uniformizer.
